**FDATA publishes governance framework for AI agents in open finance**

*The proposals set out principles for how autonomous AI agents should operate within regulated financial data-sharing frameworks, ahead of anticipated rulemaking in the UK and EU.*

The Financial Data and Technology Association (FDATA) has published a white paper outlining a governance framework for agentic fintech, addressing how AI agents that initiate financial transactions or access account data on behalf of consumers should be supervised, authenticated and held accountable.

The paper arrives as policymakers in both the UK and EU are developing open finance rules that will need to account for AI-enabled financial services. The FCA's July AI review explicitly placed agentic payments within its supervisory scope, and the Euro Banking Association published its own mapping of agentic AI's role in open finance in June. FDATA's framework attempts to pre-empt fragmented national approaches by proposing common principles around consent delegation, liability and audit trails for agent-initiated actions.

The white paper closes with a set of recommendations directed at regulators and standard-setting bodies, arguing that existing open banking consent models were not designed for autonomous agents and will require adaptation rather than simple extension. Whether regulators adopt FDATA's framing or develop their own remains to be seen, but the trade body's intervention adds specificity to a debate that has so far been largely conceptual.

*Sources: [FDATA white paper outlines agentic fintech governance](https://thepaypers.com/fintech/news/fdata-calls-for-agentic-fintech-governance-framework) — The Paypers*

stories.original:
**Mastercard frames open finance as global infrastructure, not domestic plumbing**

*Cross-border data portability and interoperable standards are now central to the network's open finance positioning, signalling an ambition to operate as a global intermediary layer.*

Mastercard has set out a public case for treating open finance as scalable global infrastructure rather than a collection of domestic data-sharing regimes. In an interview with Valor International, the company argued that interoperable systems and common standards are required for open finance to move beyond its current applications in credit portability and account aggregation toward cross-border use cases.

The framing reflects Mastercard's broader strategic trajectory. The network has joined the European Payments Council, completed Europe's first agentic payment with ING and Worldline, and integrated stablecoin settlement into its merchant network, all in the first half of 2025. Positioning open finance as a cross-border infrastructure play rather than a regulatory compliance exercise gives Mastercard a rationale for embedding itself as an intermediary layer between national regimes.

For European banks and fintechs, the message is pointed. Domestic open banking frameworks in the UK and EU were designed primarily for national markets. Mastercard is arguing that the next phase of value creation lies in connecting those frameworks internationally, and that card networks are better placed than most to do so.

*Sources: [Global systems make open finance scalable and efficient, Mastercard says](https://valorinternational.globo.com/business/news/2026/08/03/global-systems-make-open-finance-scalable-and-efficient-mastercard-says.ghtml) — Valorinternational*

stories.original:
**Cover Genius acquires Friendsurance to embed insurance via open banking rails**

*The deal gives the embedded insurance platform access to PSD2-based distribution architecture across European banking, extending open banking's footprint beyond payments and lending.*

Cover Genius, the Australian embedded insurance platform, is acquiring Berlin-based Friendsurance to accelerate distribution of insurance products through European banking channels. Friendsurance's architecture incorporates PSD2 open banking rails and a framework designed to navigate European regulatory requirements, giving Cover Genius a ready-made integration path into bank apps and digital channels across the region.

The acquisition illustrates how open banking infrastructure originally built for payments and account data is being repurposed for adjacent financial products. Friendsurance has operated as an embedded insurance distributor within banking apps, using open banking connections to streamline onboarding and data retrieval. Cover Genius, which provides protection products embedded at the point of sale across travel, logistics and e-commerce, gains a European regulatory footprint and a banking-native distribution channel it did not previously have.

For European banks, the deal is a practical example of the open finance thesis in action: third parties building product layers on top of bank-held data and distribution, with insurance following the path already established by payments and lending.

*Sources: [Cover Genius to accelerate embedded protection across European banking ...](https://www.reinsurancene.ws/cover-genius-to-accelerate-embedded-protection-across-european-banking-with-friendsurance-acquisition/) — Reinsurance News*

stories.original:
**Teya launches card machine with instant merchant settlement across Europe**

*Teya Pro processes most transactions in 1.7 seconds and settles funds to merchant accounts immediately, bundling instant settlement as a default feature rather than a premium add-on.*

European SME acquirers are under growing pressure to differentiate beyond price, and Teya is responding with hardware that makes instant settlement standard. The company has launched Teya Pro, a card machine that completes the majority of transactions in 1.7 seconds and moves funds to merchants' accounts at the point of sale. The product is available across the European markets where Teya operates.

Instant settlement for merchants has historically been offered as an optional, fee-bearing service by acquirers. Teya's decision to bundle it into its standard hardware proposition reflects competitive dynamics in the European SME acquiring market. It also aligns with the broader infrastructure shift driven by the EU's instant payments regulation, which is normalising real-time money movement across the payments chain.

For incumbent acquirers, the implication is clear: as instant settlement becomes table stakes at the point of sale, the traditional float-based revenue model for merchant services comes under further pressure.

*Sources: [Teya unveils new payments card machine](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110547/teya-unveils-new-payments-card-machine?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
